cohort: Women who gave birth in Washington State from 1987 through 2011.
finding: Mothers of newborns with low birth weight had a three-fold increased risk of postpartum venous thromboembolism (VTE) compared to mothers of newborns with normal birth weight, while mothers of newborns with high birth weight had only a slightly increased risk that was attenuated after multivariable adjustment.
birth_weight: Low birth weight (<2500 g), normal birth weight (2500-4000 g), high birth weight (>4000 g)
